scenes.visual: Title card 'Same Auxin, Opposite Bends' over a seedling lying on its side, shoot curling up and root curling down, a GREY down-arrow beside it. Reuses the first film's COLOUR MAP, same in both films and the lesson figures: auxin = GOLD dots (a GOLD band where it piles up); light = BLUE arrow; lit flank PALE GREEN; shaded flank WARM ORANGE; gravity = GREY down-arrow; PIN carriers = small TEAL gates on cell faces; starch statoliths = dark BROWN grains. Seedlings are simple cartoons, cream background, 16:9. Every number and date appears only as on-screen text. Anything not computed is labelled 'schematic'. Growth curves: shoot curve WARM ORANGE, root curve DEEP BROWN.

scenes.tts: Lay a seedling on its side. Its shoot turns up, and its root turns down. Yet both gather auxin on their lower side. How can one signal give opposite bends?
scenes.visual: A seedling rotates to horizontal. A GREY down-arrow appears. Over time the shoot curls upward and the root curls downward. A GOLD band forms along the lower edge of both, with a question mark.
scenes.narration: Lay a seedling on its side. Its shoot turns up, and its root turns down. Yet both gather auxin on their lower side. How can one signal give opposite bends?

scenes.tts: The first film showed light moving auxin to the shaded flank, which grew faster. Gravity moves auxin too. Same gold dots, new direction. This time, though, the shoot and the root disagree.
scenes.visual: Brief replay: the first film's two-column shoot with GOLD dots sliding to the WARM ORANGE flank under a BLUE arrow. The BLUE arrow swings round and becomes the GREY down-arrow; the GOLD dots now slide downward.
scenes.narration: The first film showed light moving auxin to the shaded flank, which grew faster. Gravity moves auxin too. Same gold dots, new direction. This time, though, the shoot and the root disagree.

scenes.tts: First, the plant must sense which way is down. In the root cap, central cells called columella cells hold plastids packed with dense starch.
scenes.visual: Zoom into a root tip. The cap's central cells glow, label 'columella cells'. Inside one cell, dark BROWN grains rest on the floor, label 'plastids packed with starch'.
scenes.narration: First, the plant must sense which way is down. In the root cap, central cells called columella cells hold plastids packed with dense starch.

scenes.tts: Turn the root on its side, and these heavy plastids sink to the new floor of each cell. They act as statoliths, one of the root's gravity sensors.
scenes.visual: The columella cell rotates 90 degrees. The BROWN grains slide and settle onto the new lower wall. Label 'statoliths: one gravity sensor'.
scenes.narration: Turn the root on its side, and these heavy plastids sink to the new floor of each cell. They act as statoliths, one of the root's gravity sensors.

scenes.tts: Auxin leaves cells through carriers called PIN proteins. In Arabidopsis root-cap cells, one carrier, PIN three, moves quickly to the new lower face.
scenes.caption: Auxin leaves cells through carriers called PIN proteins. In Arabidopsis root-cap cells, one carrier, PIN3, moves quickly to the new lower face.
scenes.visual: Small TEAL gates labelled 'PIN3' sit around the cell. After the rotation they slide along the membrane and cluster on the lower face. GOLD dots exit through them, downward. Caption 'Arabidopsis'.
scenes.narration: Auxin leaves cells through carriers called PIN proteins. In Arabidopsis root-cap cells, one carrier, PIN3, moves quickly to the new lower face.

scenes.tts: So auxin flows toward the lower side of the root. In the shoot, extra auxin gathers along the lower flank too.
scenes.visual: Zoom out: GOLD dots stream into the lower flank of the horizontal root and build a GOLD band. The horizontal shoot also gets a GOLD band along its lower flank.
scenes.narration: So auxin flows toward the lower side of the root. In the shoot, extra auxin gathers along the lower flank too.

scenes.tts: You met the rule at the start of the lesson. Now apply it to the root. Auxin piles up on its lower flank. Does that flank grow faster or slower than the top?
scenes.visual: The horizontal root alone, GOLD band on its lower flank, two arrows 'faster?' and 'slower?' on the lower flank, question card.
scenes.narration: You met the rule at the start of the lesson. Now apply it to the root. Auxin piles up on its lower flank. Does that flank grow faster or slower than the top?

scenes.visual: Predict pause. Question card holds; a 5-second ring timer counts down.

scenes.tts: Slower. In the root, this auxin inhibits elongation of the lower epidermal cells. The upper flank outgrows it, and the root curves down.
scenes.visual: The root's lower surface cells, label 'epidermal cells', lengthen only a little; upper ones lengthen more. The root tip curves down toward the GREY arrow.
scenes.narration: Slower. In the root, this auxin inhibits elongation of the lower epidermal cells. The upper flank outgrows it, and the root curves down.

scenes.tts: In the shoot, extra auxin speeds elongation of the lower flank. So the shoot curves up.
scenes.visual: The shoot's lower flank, GOLD band, lengthens more than the upper; the shoot tip lifts upward, away from the GREY arrow.
scenes.narration: In the shoot, extra auxin speeds elongation of the lower flank. So the shoot curves up.

scenes.tts: Why opposite answers? Plot growth against auxin level for each organ. Each curve rises to a peak, then falls.
scenes.visual: Axes: horizontal 'auxin level (log scale)', vertical 'growth'. A WARM ORANGE bell curve labelled 'shoot' draws itself, then a DEEP BROWN bell curve labelled 'root'. Both computed from one simple bell-shaped model; label 'schematic shapes and positions'. No numbers on either axis.
scenes.narration: Why opposite answers? Plot growth against auxin level for each organ. Each curve rises to a peak, then falls.

scenes.tts: Roots respond to much lower auxin levels than shoots. So the root's curve sits far to the left.
scenes.visual: The DEEP BROWN root curve slides far to the left of the WARM ORANGE shoot curve; a double-headed arrow between their peaks reads 'far lower auxin for roots'. No numbers on the axis.
scenes.narration: Roots respond to much lower auxin levels than shoots. So the root's curve sits far to the left.

scenes.tts: Where does each organ work on its curve? In the classic picture, a shoot works on its rising slope. There, more auxin means faster growth.
scenes.visual: A single GOLD marker sits on the rising slope of the WARM ORANGE shoot curve. It slides a little to the right and rises; beside the plot the shoot's lower flank lengthens and the shoot lifts. Label 'position assumed (schematic)'.
scenes.narration: Where does each organ work on its curve? In the classic picture, a shoot works on its rising slope. There, more auxin means faster growth.

scenes.tts: A root works past its peak. There, more auxin means slower growth. So the same kind of signal gives opposite bends.
scenes.visual: A separate GOLD marker sits on the falling side of the DEEP BROWN root curve. It slides a little to the right and drops; beside the plot the root's lower flank lags and the root curves down. Label 'position assumed (schematic)'. The two markers are never joined by a shared line and never take equal steps.
scenes.narration: A root works past its peak. There, more auxin means slower growth. So the same kind of signal gives opposite bends.

scenes.tts: But these curves give the sign of each bend, not its cause. Each tissue turns auxin into growth in its own way. Why roots are so sensitive is still not fully explained.
scenes.visual: The two curves dim; the label 'sign, not cause' sits over them. Small tags: 'each tissue has its own growth machinery' and 'gravity sensing worked out in Arabidopsis seedlings'.
scenes.narration: But these curves give the sign of each bend, not its cause. Each tissue turns auxin into growth in its own way. Why roots are so sensitive is still not fully explained.

scenes.tts: The plant is not reaching for anything. Light or gravity, the rule is the same. The plant moves auxin to one flank. That flank grows faster in a shoot, and slower in a root.
scenes.visual: Recap: settled BROWN statoliths, TEAL PIN3 gates on the lower face, the GOLD band, and the shoot up and root down.
scenes.narration: The plant is not reaching for anything. Light or gravity, the rule is the same. The plant moves auxin to one flank. That flank grows faster in a shoot, and slower in a root.

scenes.visual: End card with Hex. LINE: 'More auxin on the lower flank: shoots grow faster there, roots slower.'
